verdict.rationale: Adyen's relayed authorisation sends a webhook with transaction data for each authorisation request. Your server replies with an approval or refusal within a documented 2000 ms window, and if it doesn't reply in time you configure the fallback yourself (default approval or default refusal). Every element of the story is covered by first-party docs. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the relayed authorisation flow and its timeout behavior.

support.subject: As a developer, I can approve or decline each authorization in real time — a webhook or auth-stream endpoint my code answers inside the network's time budget, with a documented timeout fallback I control

citations.quote: With each relayed authorisation webhook we send, you have up to 2000 milliseconds to reply with an approval or a refusal.
If you do not respond within 2000 milliseconds, you can specify which fallback logic you want: Default approval, Default refusal
When we receive a payment authorisation request, we send you a relayed authorisation webhook with the relevant transaction data, including transaction rules and validation checks.
Relayed authorisation allows you to make a real-time decision on whether to approve or decline a transaction.
